type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : SeminormedRing R] {f : Polynomial R} {A : ℝ},
  (∀ (i : ℕ), ‖f.coeff i‖ ≤ A) →
    ∀ (P : Polynomial R) {C : ℝ},
      (∀ (i : ℕ), ‖P.coeff i‖ ≤ C) →
        ∀ {s : ℕ}, P.natDegree ≤ s → ∀ (i : ℕ), ‖(P %ₘ f).coeff i‖ ≤ (1 + A) ^ (s + 1 - f.natDegree) * C
what: Every coefficient of the monic-division remainder is bounded by (1+A)^(s+1-f.natDegree) C, with natural subtraction saturating at zero.
how: Strong degree induction combines private exists_norm_coeff_reduction_aux with Polynomial.div_wf_lemma: one leading-term elimination lowers degree and multiplies a coefficient bound by at most 1+A.
hypotheses: An arbitrary seminormed ring, coefficient bounds A and C for f and P, and P.natDegree≤s; no monicity, nontriviality or sign premises.
caller_summary: One explicit body caller, private abs_coeff_diag_hasseDeriv_modByMonic_le_aux at MainLemma:512; zero external-to-file or direct type consumers. Fullmodule caller reroute to new generic size estimate compiles with original signature.
mathlib_api_audit: Existing division and norm building blocks do not supply the quantitative iteration. CoeffMem gives algebraic submodule membership, not bounds on archimedean size; GaussNorm/supNorm provide alternative representations.
moral_duplications: The private reduction is one step of this theorem; diagonal Hasse remainder estimate is a genuine downstream specialization, not a duplicate. Factor/root bounds are different statements.
generalization: Verified mathlib-only Ring R and arbitrary v:R→ℝ with v0=0, nonnegativity, sub triangle and submultiplicativity, preserving s+1-f.natDegree. This is a newly proved size_remainder, not existing mathlib. Bundled RingSeminorm alternative is source-inspected, not claimed compile-verified; no extra import authorization received.
missing_api: Quantitative coefficient growth under iterated monic reduction; choice of direct norm, bundled seminorm or supNorm public interface remains upstream design.
junk: Not removable as a ≤3-existing-mathlib-call wrapper; the only local caller can use the new generic theorem but that is a new proof. Local direct inlining hit default limits and is not a deletion recommendation.
